abstract: The self-contained oil-filled cable has been developed to meet increasing power requirements both in terms of voltage and ampacity. The paper gives details of power transmission capability for 230, 345 and 525 kV cable systems for a variety of natural and forced cooled conditions. The highest rating is obtained with internal oil cooling and at 525kV 4000 MVA can be transmitted using one cable per phase. Details are given of accessory design features that have been adopted to ensure that these components do not become a limitation to power transmission capability.

articleTitle: A Theoretical Analysis of Dynamic Arcs and Test Results of Model Synchronous Air Blast Circuit Breakers
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper reported analyzed results of the transient dynamic arc around current zero of air blast circuit breakers on the basis of Mayr arc model. It was proved that an arc time constant and arc power loss were determined by boundary layer flow analysis just around current zero. By these arc constants, max. RRRV P1-5/(di/dt)20 (P: Pressure, (di/dt)o : current derivative without arc). These proprieties were confirmed by experimental results of the model synchronous air blast circuit breaker. Moreover, the water flow with open surface was applied to analyze dependence of time constant on the geometrical form and arrangement of arc quenching nozzles.

articleTitle: Seismic Design Guidelines for Substation Facilities
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper discusses one utility's seismic design guidelines for assuring continuity of service at substation facilities during and after future earthquakes. Presented is an aggregate analysis of a five-year research and development program conducted by the Southern California Edison Company (SCE) in order to determine the seismic properties and withstand capability of critical substation components. The most significant aspect of these seismic design procedures is the incorporation of cost/risk considerations early in the design effort.

articleTitle: A Premolded Splice for 138KV Extruded Dielectric Cable
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: A premolded splice for 138kV extruded dielectric cable was developed in a project sponsored by EPRI and ERDA. The splices offer significant advantages in ease of assembly and in reliability as a result of pretesting at the factory.

articleTitle: state-Space Modeling oif a Series Compensated Long Distance Transmission System Through Graph-Theoretic Approach
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The paper demonstrates a powerful application of graph-theoretic approach in developing a linearized state-model for a typical hydro- power system effectively and systematically. The linearized d-q state models of basic components of power system such as generator, transformer, transmission line are formulated (conceptually, in isolation) in a synchronousiy rotating frame which permits ease of inter- connection without involving any intermediary of axis transformations. The formulation of model in general, is applicable to multi- machine system and is easily amenable to digital simulation. It is hoped that the system state-model formulation through graph-the- oretic approach would strongly appeal to power system engineers engaged in large-scale comprehensive dynamical system studies.

articleTitle: Design Features for Reference Coal Fueled Generating Station Auxiliary Electric Power Systems
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Gilbert/Commonwealth (G/C) has developed a reference design of an auxiliary electric power system for use in 500 MW to 800 MW coal-fired plants. As a reference design, it may be adapted to a wide range of variables such as climate, fuel, and major equipment manufacturers. A typical 650 MW unit is described along with its major equipment parameters and design layout, construction, and operation. Whenever the design varies with different megawatt ratings, these variations will be described. The application of a generator load break switch is presented. Its use allows the generator stepup transformer to be the source of auxiliary power for unit startup and shutdown.

articleTitle: Heat Conduction in the Cable Insulation Forced-Cooled Underground Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Forced cooling of pipe type transmission systems permits a substantial increase in their current capacity. To accurately predict the operating temperature within forced cooled cables, the conduction heat transfer within the insulation must be accurately modeled. In particular, hot spots due to the proximity of one cable to another, or to the pipe wall must be considered.

articleTitle: Scaling Criteria for Interruption Performance in Gas-Blast Circuit-Breakers
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The high cost and complexity of short-circuit interruption testing of gas-blast power circuit-breakers make it essential to use most efficiently results of reduced power development tests in interrupter design. Due to the limited capacity of direct testing stations many EHV-breakers must be evaluated by indirect methods such as synthetic-testing of single interrupter units. The interpretation of synthetic-test data and the effective utilization of reduced power test data in circuit-breaker design can be enhanced by the development of accurate scaling criteria. The present paper demonstrates to what extend scaling of enthalpy-flow, current density, pressure, interruption capability, nozzle area ratio, contact spacing, and shape factors can extend the results of reduced power experimental tests to predict performance at full short-circuit ratings.

articleTitle: Synthetic Methods for Testing of Vacuum Breakers
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Different synthetic methods are scrutinized as to the applicability to vacuum breakers. Skeats method with resistor is brought forward and discussed from the viewpoint of breaker failure modes, interruption and circuit phenomena. Criteria for choice of resistor are given. Comparison tests using this method and direct method were performed. The results support theoretical conclusions by experimental verification of equivalency for the tested vacuum breaker. The method offers practical and economical advantages over current injection and is also suitable for multiloop and duty cycle testing.

articleTitle: Electric Power Engineering Educational Resources--1975-76
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This fourth biennial(1,2,3,4) committee report covers results of a survey of Electric Power Engineering Educational Resources at ECPD (Engineers Council for Professional Development) accredited universities in the United States of America for the academic year 1975-1976. This report includes a listing of faculty active during the subject year, their level of academic involvement and professional experience, together with information on undergraduate student enrollment in various subject matter. Also included is information concerning graduate student enrollment in various subject matter, degrees granted and research- funding support activity.

articleTitle: Short -- Circuit Temperature Ratings of Buried Extruded Dielectric Cables
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper describes a computer program which can calculate the steady state and. transient temperature distribution in underground extruded dielectric power cables. The transient, conditions are assumed to be caused by short-conditions and the subsequent circuit breaker reclosure cycles. The program is a design tool that can be used to predict cable properties, geometries and operating conditions which can lead to safe temperatures under steady and transient conditions. The analysis results from an energy balance on up to four cable materials and the earth. The energy equation is solved by an implicit finite difference technique. The analysis includes dielectric losses, skin effect, circulating shield currents and mutual heating between cables. Both steady state and transient results are compared with available data.

articleTitle: Modification and Performance Evaluation of the Faster-Than-Real-Time Hybrid Simulator
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The basic capability of the long term dynamics hybrid simulator was described in the RP908-1 final Report [1], [2]. As a part of the RP908-2 project, the capability of the simulator has been improved and expanded [3] The generator model was improved to a two axis model allowing the full representation of the subtransient and transient reactance values. The generator model now adequately represents the short term dynamics as well as the long term dynamics.

articleTitle: UHV Disconnectors: Switching Surge Design and Testing of External Insulation
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The switching surge insulation characteristics of a disconnector (formerly "switch") are presented in a generalized form, based on a series of tests performed on UHV disconnectors with various heights H and clearances between contacts D. The knowledge of these characteristics and of the distribution of the expected overvoltages in service allows to determine the total risk of discharge RT and the risk of discharge across the longitudinal insulation RL. A general method for the design of a disconnector that meets prescribed maximum tolerable risks is presented. The statistical significance of a type test is then investigated, and the procedures recommended by IEC and IEEE are criticized. Some changes in the testing procedure are finally proposed, in order to ameliorate the tests and to reduce the differences between their requirements on the design of a disconnector.

articleTitle: Central Computer Control and Protection Functions
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Planning and equipment selection for a central computer or computer complex begins with its intended functions.

articleTitle: A Method of Generating Four-Parameter Transient Recovery Voltage During Synthetic Tests of Large Capacity Circuit Breakers
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This report relates to how to make up a synthetic test circuit that is designed to generate four-parameter transient recovery voltage during a breaking performance test of large capacity circuit breakers, The report also refers to how to determine constants of the elements that compose the test circuit, as well as its inherent characteristics.

articleTitle: Computational Implementation of On-Line Loadflow
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper describes a straightforward building method of initializing internal and external network system bus voltage and power injection operating levels for subsequent steady-state system security evaluation of planned and unplanned network contingency outages. Outages are of the line, tie-line, generator, or load loss type. The program can handle the opening of bus tie or jumper connections and the isolation of a bus or string of buses from the main part of the network. The routine's main advantage is the automatic redistribution and makeup of tie-line P (MW) and Q (Mvar) flows from the external network. This algorithm has been implemented on the Iowa Illinois Gas and Electric Company (IIG&E) real-time control system; it is now under test and evaluation, and preliminary results are most favorable.

articleTitle: An Updated List of Current Operational Problems
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper is one of a series prepared by the Current Operational Problems (COPs) Working Group with the goal of focusing the attention of industry problem solvers on high priority problems faced by those who are involved in the actual operation of power systems.

articleTitle: Asynchronous Operation of A. C. Synchronous Machines The Linear Equivalent Circuit
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: An equivalent circuit is derived for analyzing the behavior of a linear synchronous machine operating asynchronously. It permits the calculation of all torques and all voltage and current harmonics for any slip with respect to a given stator fundamental frequency input. Relationships to previously reported equations or to supporting analyses are given.

articleTitle: Bibliography of Relay Literature, 1974-1975
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: THE LATEST OF A SERIES OF CLASSIFIED LISTS OF POWER SYSTEM RELAY REFERENCCES, BEGUN IN 1927, IS PRESENTED.

articleTitle: Newly Developed FM Current-Differential Carrier Relaying System and its Field Experiences
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper presents the theoretical and experimental studies on the newly developed FM current- differential carrier relaying system ( FM relay). FM relay, with outstanding facility compared with any types of conventional relays, can be applied to multiterminal lines as well as two-terminal lines where conventional types of relays may not be considered satisfactory. The principle of this system lies in the current-differential protection in which the instantaneous current values at each terminal are frequency- modulated and transferred via microwave communication system. The results of a long term field test which was successfully performed on a three-terminal tapped transmission line showed the excellent performances of the FM relay.

articleTitle: Guidelines for use in Developing a Specific Underground Distribution System Design Standard
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This task group report sets forth guidelines for power distribution engineers to use when developing specific underground distribution system design standards tailored to fit their own system needs. The report consists of a system design guideline which includes a discussion of design parameters and a primer of distribution system design considerations. The objective of this guideline is to facilitate the development of economical, safe, reliable and environmentally acceptable underground distribution systems.

articleTitle: Optimal Design and Loboratory Testing of Post-Type Spacers for Three-Phase, SF6 Insulated Cables Part II Numerical Method for Controlling the Electric Field at Spacer Boundaries
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper describes a numerical method to calculate and control the electric field intensity at gas/dielectric boundaries in three-phase, gas insulated cables. It contains a detailed discription of the implementation of the optimization philosophy presented in Part I. Simplifying analytical techniques are presented leading to a computer algorithm that defines a dielectric profile which meets a maximum constraint for electric field intensity while minimizing the volume of spacer dielectric material.

articleTitle: A Model for the Study of Switching-Surge Breakdown of Long Air Gaps
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: A model of the discharge process leading to the switching surge flashover of long air gaps is presented. This model is based on a new non-thermal equilibriummodel of thedischargechannel. Dependingon temperature and current, the volt ampere characteristics of the discharge channel simulation behave either like a resistoror a zener diode. This channel simulation is combined with an electric field calculation to produce a breakdown model for arbitrary gap geometries and applied voltage waveforms. The model is currently implemented on a minicomputer system.

articleTitle: Line Entrance Protection of 500 KV Gas Insulated Substations by SF6 Spark Gaps
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The use of both station arresters and line entrance arresters provides absolute protection for all operating conditions of gas insulated substations (GIS). However, it represents a costly installation. Hence the adoption of line entrance rod gaps in air can be taken into consideration. But their protection ability is questionable because the slope of the V-t curves for air gaps is much steeper than that for GIS, while SF6 spark gaps with good sparkover characteristics would meet the requirements for the ability to protect the line entrance apparatus of GIS.

articleTitle: AEP-ASEA UHV Research Project -- Test Line and Station Design
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper will relate the AEP-ASEA UHV Test Line and Station Design by elaborating on the characteristics and details of the UHV line structures and hardware, the station layout and equipment and the reasons for their selection.

articleTitle: Incorporating Investment Opportunities into Economic Evaluations to Minimize Corporate Revenue Requirements
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: A revised methodology for performing economic evaluations is presented in this paper which incorporates an investment opportunity analysis in the conventional Minimum Revenue Requirement (MRR) Method. The method presented in this paper is termed the Minimum Revenue Requirement-Investment Opportunity Return (MRR-IOR) Method. This investment opportunity analysis minimizes revenue requirements on a corporate basis and recognizes the present environment of limited capital availability.

articleTitle: Realistic Reduction of Nonlinear Networks
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper describes a step-by-step network reduction technique which is accurate enough to provide realistic simulations of power systems with nonlinear loads. This method has been developed at Arizona State University as a part of an ongoing research program sponsored by the Electric Power Research Institute to investigate methods of economically extending transient stability simulations. Test results; from up to 49 bus examples indicate that the errors introduced by the network reduction are quite tolerable provided the angular swings and voltage deviations at retained buses are not excessive.

articleTitle: Concepts and Features of the Automated Unite Control System for the Raccoon Mountain Pumped-Storage Plant
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper describes the man-machine interface requirements, the controlled components, the operating processes, and operating restraints which apply to the Raccoon Mountain Pumped-Storage Plant. It shows how the evaluation of these factors led to a definition of the degree of automation to be achieved and, to a large extent, to the choice of controlling mechanisms to be utilized. Finally, it describes, both in concept and in function, the resulting system. which controls four of the world's largest reversible pump-turbines.

articleTitle: Development in New Type High Response Excitation System for Improved Power System Stability
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper introduces a high initial response excitation system with a new type automatic voltage regulator which consists of two signal processing circuits. One responds to any type of disturbance and the other responds only to large diturbances. The excellent performance data verified by computor simulations and model system tests are shown below.

articleTitle: An Initial Comparative Analysis of the Market Penetration Potential of Coal and Coal Derived Fuels in the U.S. Utility Industry (1985-2005)
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: In 1972, the U.S. electric utility industry established a focal point for all of the industry's research and development efforts by forming the Electric Power Research Institute (EPRI). When EPRI began, there was no alternative to relatively subjective judgment in allocating our research and development resources among competing power generation, transmission, and distribution technologies. During the last two years, we have been developing a more quantitative analytical approach to estimate the relative market penetration potential of alternative power generation systems. This paper focuses on one of these analyses; namely, a generation expansion analysis which compares the economics of various electric utility alternatives for coal utilization in the period 1985-2005. Although this is only a first iteration, the methodology developed and initial results are deemed significant.

articleTitle: Flow and Heat Transfer in the Water-Cooled Rotor Winding of a Turbine Generator
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Detailed investigation of flow and heat transfer in revolving coolant conduits was made to establish the methd of prediction of required pump capacity and winding tempreratue. The non-dimensional parameters which govern the flows in essential parts of the coolant path are shown. They provide the designers with a method of design analysis having generality and physical, reasoning. Measurement of pressure drop and winding temperature in the rotor of a two-pole prototype generator confirmed the present prediction method.

articleTitle: Controlling Noise in a Large Steam Turbine-Generator Room
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The Long Island Lighting Company was recently the recipient of the first National Environmental Award for outstanding achievement in noise abatement, as a result of noise control measurements employed in its Northport power station.

articleTitle: Mathematical Theory of Longitudinally Loaded Elastic-Plastic Transmission Lines -- Statics
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: A complete mathematical model is presented to predict the longitudinal strength of a transmission-line system. This is the first presentation of such a unified model. The static equilibrium of a generalized system subjected to broken wires, unbalanced ice, or longitudinal wind (taken separately or in combination) is determined. Emphasis is given to longitudinal wind and extreme loading conditions requiring structural deflections beyond the elastic limit. Theory is compared to experimental findings, and new results demonstrating design tradeoffs for wind loading and large foundation movements are presented.

articleTitle: Design of the Proposed ± 400 KV DC Gull Island Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The paper discusses the design methods and parameters for a ±400 kV dc transmission line proposed for the Gull Island Power Development.

articleTitle: Bibliography on Power Capacitors 1971-1974
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This report was prepared as an activity of the Capacitor Subcommittee of the IEEE Transmission and Distribution Committee to extend the existing bibliographies through the years 1971-1974. A total of 123 articles are referenced and classified, relative to economics, designs, and applications. Many foreign language papers are listed. It is the intent of the Committee to publish these reports at regular intervals to maintain a quick reference guide on contemporary power capacitor papers.

articleTitle: Performance of Extruded Dielectric (XLPE) Cable
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Samples from a 138kV XLPE cable tested at Waltz Mill are examined and compared with an unenergized piece. Several new analytical techniques are employed and studies are made concerning the distribution of discontinuities (contaminants, ambers, voids, and trees, etc.), cure-related items (extractables, density, residual peroxide and decomposition products, etc.), thermal and oxidation stability, incipient voids and trees, and shield-to-insulation smoothness. Changes are seen for many of these factors between the original and tested cable samples. Some of the effects are subtle, complex and/or unsuspected. The overall assessment for XLPE power cables, however, is encouraging.

articleTitle: Alignment, Plumbing and Bearing Adjustments for Vertical-Shaft Hydroelectric Generating Units
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper describes detailed procedures for a- lightning and plumbing vertical shaft hydro units. As- found measurements, analysis of date, corrective measures, and the adjustments of several types of bearings are described.

articleTitle: Evaluation of AC Motor Insualtion Systems by IEEE 275
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Two decades of experience at Westinghouse Large Rotating Apparatus Division evaluating motor insulation systems according to IEEE 275 and its precursor standards show good correlation between service experience on the systems tested and the conclusions drawn from the procedure. Despite its drawbacks and abuses, the test procedure has proved itself a practical and very important technique for thermal classification of insulation systems.

articleTitle: Selection of Standard Sizes for Metallic Electrical Conductors for Insulated Wires and Cables
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper discusses factors which should be considered in developing standard sizes for metallic electrical conductors to be used in insulated wires and cables. Standards for solid and stranded conductors in both the United States and International systems are analyzed and compared. In response to a growing interest in the forthcoming metrication of the U.S., guidelines for a rational and distinctive approach to standardizing metric-dimensioned conductors are offered.

articleTitle: Production Transmission System Planning at the E.D.F.
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The planning of generation means and of networks obviously depends upon effective forecasting in terms of time space, of power needs. An indication is therefore given as to how the E. D. F. provides such forecasts.

articleTitle: The LMFBR -- An International Effort
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Review of the operating experience and current status of the twenty LMFBR projects around the world establishes that substantial progress has been made in the development of the LMFBR as an alternative long-time energy source displaying high efficiency in the use of natural resources.

articleTitle: Bibliography of Operational Fixed and Mobile Radio System Literature
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: A compilation of available operational fixed and mobile radio system literature in the form of a bibliography to serve as a guide to the power utility engineer in planning a radio system.

articleTitle: 400 kV Cable Installations in Mexico
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: As a consequence of the development in the recent years of the Mexican 400 kV grid, the first two 400 kV cable installations in Mexico were carried out at Infernillo and Angostura Power Plants. In both installations self-contained oil-filled cables were chosen. After a general description of the plants, the cable and accessory design is discussed. Particular reference is made to laying problems, especially for the Angostura 130 m vertical shaft installation.

articleTitle: The Loy Yang 4000 MW Brown Coal Power Development
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The paper covers the need for a major base load brown coal power project in the 1980' s and discusses the planning and some economic, technical and environmental aspects including public participation.

articleTitle: An Optimal Ordering Algorithm for Sparse Matrix Applications
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper presents a new, optimal (according to a criterion defined later), sparsity-oriented, ordering algorithm for application in sparse matrix calculations. A dynamic programming algorithm which determines an ordered elimination such that the total number of fill-in terms is minimum is developed. The ordering algorithm is shown to be better, i.e. less fill-in, than the clustering method of reference [4]. The algorithm, is valid for diagonally dominant matrices which are symmetric in pattern of nonzero elements. The method has been found practical for ordering matrices appearing in a wide variety of engineering applications. Presently, it can be efficiently applied to matrices of the order of 50 rows.

articleTitle: Computation of Transient Temperatures and Pressures in Oil Filled Cables
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: A calculation method has been developed for the transient temperatures and pressures in oil filled cables. The method models the thermal and pressure fields as two coupled resistance-capacitance electrical networks. This conceptually simple analog is extended to include the effects of cable-sheath elasticity, oil compressibility and sheath thermal expansion. The variation of surrounding temperature along the route and changes of oil viscosity and copper resistance with temperature are considered. The method has been implemented as a computer program and applied to the analysis of an 18 km HVdc cable system in a deep tunnel.

articleTitle: Lightning and the Perth-Geraldton 132 KV Line
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Although in an area of low to moderate thunderstorm activity, the design and operation of the 440 kM 132 kV line from Perth to Geraldton was largely controlled by the lightning. An unusual design, with structures consisting of three independent 23.6 m (50 feet) poles, was developed to utilise the arc quenching properties of wood to achieve a reasonable lightning performance without recourse to the provision of overhead earthwires. The paper describes the line design, the first three years of operating experience, and presents a detailed comparison between the observed and predicted frequency of lightning strikes, flashovers and damage to the line.

articleTitle: Vol. PAS-97 1978 Index IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This index covers all technical items - papers, correspondence, reviews, etc. - that appeared in this periodical during the year, and items from previous years that were commented upon or corrected in this year. Departments and other items may also be covered if they have been judged to have archival value. The Author Index contains the primary entry for each item, listed under the first author's name. The primary entry includes the coauthors' names, the title of the paper or other item, and its location, specified by the publication abbreviation, year, month, and inclusive pagination. The Subject Index contains entries describing the item under all appropriate subject headings, plus the first author's name, the publication abbreviation, month, and year, and inclusive pages. Note that the item title is found only under the primary entry in the Author Index.
